clauses_raw.clause_text_raw: The RN zone is intended to permit single-detached and semi-detached dwellings up to 4 units per lot (with conditions) and complementary forms of uses that maintain community residential character (accessory dwelling uses, home occupations, home daycare, etc.).
Rezoning from RN to RM may be considered where the policies of the Official Plan can be demonstrated, otherwise, rezonings are not permitted in the RN Zone.
The following uses are permitted in the RN Zone:
Government Offices
Library
Semi Detached Dwelling
Single Detached Dwelling
These uses are permitted provided that the following lot requirements are met:
Existing lots with frontage greater than 18 m shall not be subdivided except with an approved variance.

clauses_raw.clause_text_raw: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) permissions:
One or two attached ADUs may be permitted if the conditions in Section 4.6 can be met; and
One rear-yard or side-yard detached ADU may be permitted if the conditions in Section 4.7 can be met.

Notwithstanding Sections 10.3.1, 10.4.1(a), 4.6.2 and 4.6.3, a designated heritage buildings on a lot with an area exceeding 600 m² permit up to 6 attached ADUs, subject to the following requirements:
the conversion is authorized through a Heritage Permit issued in accordance with the Heritage Preservation Bylaw;
the dwelling units are located within the existing heritage building, except for an addition expressly approved through the Heritage Permit process;
the development complies with applicable building, fire, water and sewer requirements;
parking is provided in accordance with Part 8;
no additional attached or detached accessory dwelling unit or secondary suite is permitted on the lot;
any short-term rental use complies with Section 4.11 and is limited to no more than one dwelling unit on the lot; and
all other applicable requirements of this bylaw are satisfied.
Permitted encroachments into the setbacks are listed in Table 3.2.
Home occupations are permitted if Section 4.9 requirements are met.
Home daycare uses are permitted if Section 4.10 requirements are met.
Notwithstanding Section 10.3.1, manufactured housing uses are permitted in the areas shown in Schedule 10.1 provided that the following requirements are met:

clauses_raw.clause_text_raw: One building per lot is permitted.
The maximum building height for the RN zone is 3 storeys.
Any garage (attached or detached) shall not project any closer to the streetline than the longest wall of the attached main dwelling that faces the same streetline.
Attached garages shall not exceed 50% of the primary building's frontage on any streetline to a maximum of 6 m in total.
Developers are encouraged to use materials and styles consistent with existing neighbourhood character.
To discourage excessive repetition of identical home designs within the same street block the following requirements must be met:
New residential development shall exhibit a variety of building designs 4 m2 Landscaping 1.5 m Walkway along each block to reinforce individual identity and neighbourhood character.
The same dwelling design, including mirrored variations, shall not appear more than twice within any street block.
Developments proposing repeated models shall vary at least two of the following elements between dwellings:
Exterior cladding material;
Roof form or pitch;
Porch or entry design;
Window placement; or
Garage placement and style
The Development Officer may approve alternative approaches that achieve an equivalent degree of architectural diversity.

To enhance streetscape interest and avoid flat wall surfaces, all street-facing facades shall include horizontal or vertical modulation of at least 150 mm in depth across no less than 20% of the facade area.

All disturbed surfaces shall be seeded, sodded or hydroseeded with grass or meadow mixture or restored to natural condition. Seeding mixes must not include PEI invasive species.
All driveways shall be hard surfaced with asphalt, concrete or unit pavers. Loose gravel or soil is not permitted.
Parking in the front yard is only permitted on hard-surfaced driveways or parking spots.
No more than 40% of the front yard area can be driveway or parking spaces.
No less than 4 (min. 2 m high) trees shall be planted on each lot or 1 per manufactured home for units in Schedule 10.1 areas.
No less than 4 m2 of shrub beds shall be planted in the front yard consisting of shrubs, annuals or perennials.

Where manufactured housing directly abuts the property line of any other housing type in the RN zone, a landscape buffer consisting of a minimum 1.8 m high opaque fence, and one tree (min. 2 m high) for every 8 m of abutting side or rear yard shall be installed.
